subject: Confidential deployment discovery — recap & next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Confidential deployment discovery — recap & next steps

Hi Lena / David,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the open conversation about Aurelia's constrained hosting and regulatory requirements. I wanted to capture what we heard and outline clear next steps so we can move at the right pace for procurement.

Summary of main points you raised:
- Primary driver: maintain patient-data residency in the EU and eliminate any uncontrolled egress.
- Operational constraint: must be deployable into an air-gapped facility with only deliberate, auditable update windows (no persistent internet egress).
- Security bar: SOC 2 plus ISO 27001 preferred; ability to integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM.
- Networking: strict allowlist, no direct public egress, support for private peering or VPN with explicit NAT/egress controls.
- Timeline: budget window opens Q1 2027; evaluation/PO decision targeted by end of Feb 2027.

Technical uncertainties we flagged that we need to confirm:
- Update path for model weights and security patches for an air-gapped deployment (encrypted transfer cadence, signing).
- Support for customer HSM (PKCS#11) vs Redwood-managed KMS options.
- Required on-prem hardware profile (GPU/CPU mix) and whether a single on-prem host can meet low-latency needs for the initial pilot.
- Network topology: whether you can provision a private VPC peering or if we should design a jumpbox transfer process.

Agreed next steps (owner / ETA):
1) Redwood to share call notes & initial security questionnaire (attached) — Grace — EOD 2026-11-01.
2) Aurelia to confirm offline-update constraints (allowed media, signing requirements) and an initial list of compliance docs (SOC2/ISO) — Lena — by 2026-11-05.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Aurelia infra + Redwood infra (Karthik + Ben) to design a pilot architecture (30–45m) — propose slots below.
4) Redwood to surface options: (A) fully air-gapped on-prem package with manual update workflow, (B) VPC-residency with controlled egress & HSM integration; include approximate cost delta and pilot scope — Karthik/Ben — by 2026-11-06.

Proposed deep-dive windows (your timezone):
- Tue 2026-11-03 09:00–10:00 CET
- Wed 2026-11-04 14:00–15:00 CET

Attachments: 20261101-call-notes.pdf (summary + rough network sketch).

If that all looks right, I'll book the deep-dive for one of the proposed times. Thanks — keen to keep momentum.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the thorough notes — that matches our understanding. A couple clarifications from our side:

1) Air-gap/update process: we require an air-gapped runtime. Periodic model and patch updates are allowed but must follow: (a) encrypted container signed by Aurelia PKI, (b) transfer using audited removable media or an approved SFTP transfer via a controlled jump host, (c) staged verification by our security team prior to install.

2) HSM/KMS: Our preference is customer-controlled HSM (PKCS#11), but we can discuss Redwood-managed KMS if we can validate key import/export policies.

3) Compliance: we have SOC 2 Type II (reports available) and are pursuing ISO 27001 certification (expected Q2 2027). We will share the SOC 2 report and a redacted network diagram.

4) Procurement timeline: our procurement window is Q1 2027; we expect to run a pilot in Jan–Feb and move to a POC decision by late Feb.

We can do the technical deep-dive — Wed 2026-11-04 14:00 CET works for us. Please invite the infra folks.

Lena
Lena Morris

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Confidential deployment discovery — internal feasibility notes

Grace / Karthik — internal note before Wed's deep-dive: summarizing feasibility and unknowns from an infra perspective.

- Air-gapped model updates: feasible. Preferred approach is signed containers + an update agent that verifies signatures and performs atomic swap. We should supply a reference signing tool and verification steps.
- HSM integration: PKCS#11 looks straightforward for key operations; need to confirm vendor (Aurelia's HSM make/model) and whether they support remote attestation.
- Networking: if customer can provision private peering (VPN or Direct Connect equivalent) we can avoid any jumpbox. If not, design a jumpbox that only allows authenticated inbound transfers and route to the private subnet — avoids persistent egress.
- Pilot hardware: recommend 2 x A100-class GPUs (or equivalent) for a low-latency pilot if they expect 80–120 concurrent inference sessions. If throughput is lower, a single rTX-class host might suffice.

I'll prepare a short slide with tradeoffs and cost delta for the two deployment patterns for Wed.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
